questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Gulmarg, one of the most popular ski resorts in India, is located in which district of J&K?
questions.explanation: Gulmarg ('Meadow of Flowers') is located in Baramulla district at an altitude of about 2,650 m. Srinagar is the capital city where Dal Lake is located. Anantnag has Pahalgam and Verinag. Budgam has Yusmarg. Only Baramulla contains Gulmarg.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Salal Hydroelectric Project:

(i) It is located on the Chenab River in Reasi district.
(ii) Its installed capacity is 690 MW.
(iii) It is one of the largest hydroelectric projects in J&K.
(iv) It was built with Chinese assistance.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Salal HEP is on the Chenab in Reasi district (i correct). Its capacity is 690 MW (ii correct). It is among J&K's largest power projects (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — Salal was built by NHPC (National Hydroelectric Power Corporation) with Indian expertise, NOT Chinese assistance.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pahalgam is known as the 'Valley of Shepherds' and is a major tourist destination.
Reason (R): Pahalgam serves as the base camp for the annual Amarnath Yatra and offers activities like trekking, fishing, and pony rides.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Pahalgam means 'Village of Shepherds' and is a premier tourist spot. Reason (R) is correct — it's the Amarnath Yatra base and offers various adventure activities. The tourism attractions listed in (R) explain WHY it's a major destination (A). Option B is wrong because (R) explains the tourism appeal. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following power projects in J&K with the rivers they are located on:

Column I:
(a) Uri-I
(b) Baglihar
(c) Kishanganga
(d) Dulhasti

Column II:
(i) Chenab
(ii) Jhelum
(iii) Kishanganga (Neelum)
(iv) Chenab

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Uri-I (480 MW) is on the Jhelum River near Uri town (a-ii). Baglihar dam is on the Chenab in Doda (b-i). Kishanganga HEP (330 MW) is on the Kishanganga/Neelum river (c-iii). Dulhasti (390 MW) is on the Chenab (d-iv). Option B swaps Uri with Kishanganga. Option C mismatches Baglihar. Option D incorrectly places Uri on Chenab.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are famous Mughal Gardens located in Srinagar?

(i) Shalimar Bagh
(ii) Nishat Bagh
(iii) Chashme Shahi
(iv) Tulip Garden

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh (built by Jahangir), Nishat Bagh (by Asaf Khan), and Chashme Shahi (during Shah Jahan's reign) are all Mughal-era gardens (i, ii, iii correct). The Tulip Garden (Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden) is a MODERN garden developed in 2007, not a Mughal garden (iv incorrect).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Vaishno Devi shrine, one of India's most visited pilgrimage destinations, is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi shrine is located in the Trikuta Mountains in Reasi district (earlier Katra was part of Udhampur/Jammu, but after reorganization it falls under Reasi). Jammu city is the base for travel. Udhampur is a neighbouring district. Kathua is in southern Jammu division.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Uri-I Hydroelectric Power Project:

(i) It has an installed capacity of 480 MW.
(ii) It is located on the Jhelum River in Baramulla district.
(iii) It is a run-of-the-river project.
(iv) It was built by Pakistan as part of the Indus Waters Treaty.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Uri-I has 480 MW capacity (i correct). It's on the Jhelum near Uri town, Baramulla (ii correct). It is a run-of-the-river project as allowed under the Indus Waters Treaty (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — it was built by INDIA (NHPC), not Pakistan. India is permitted to build run-of-river projects on western rivers under the Treaty.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Gulmarg Gondola is one of the highest cable car projects in the world.
Reason (R): The Gondola's second phase reaches Apharwat Peak at approximately 3,980 metres, offering views of the Himalayan range and access to skiing slopes.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Gulmarg Gondola is among the world's highest cable cars. Reason (R) is correct — Phase 2 reaches ~3,980m at Apharwat Peak. The extreme altitude (R) is precisely what makes it one of the world's highest (A). Option B is wrong because the altitude data explains the ranking. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist destinations with their popular descriptions:

Column I:
(a) Sonamarg
(b) Yusmarg
(c) Gulmarg
(d) Pahalgam

Column II:
(i) Valley of Shepherds
(ii) Meadow of Gold
(iii) Meadow of Flowers
(iv) Meadow of Jesus (Issa)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Sonamarg means 'Meadow of Gold' (a-ii). Yusmarg means 'Meadow of Jesus/Issa' (b-iv). Gulmarg means 'Meadow of Flowers' (c-iii). Pahalgam means 'Valley/Village of Shepherds' (d-i). Option B swaps Sonamarg with Gulmarg. Option C mismatches Gulmarg with Pahalgam. Option D incorrectly pairs Sonamarg with Yusmarg's meaning.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The installed capacity of the Kishanganga Hydroelectric Project is:
questions.explanation: The Kishanganga HEP has an installed capacity of 330 MW. It is located on the Kishanganga (Neelum) River. 480 MW is the capacity of Uri-I. 690 MW is the capacity of Salal. 240 MW is the capacity of Uri-II.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Dal Lake in Srinagar:

(i) It is known as the 'Jewel in the Crown of Kashmir'.
(ii) The famous houseboats and shikaras are associated with this lake.
(iii) The Mughal Gardens are situated on its eastern shore along Zabarwan hills.
(iv) It is the largest freshwater lake in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is called 'Jewel in the Crown of Kashmir' (i correct). Houseboats and shikaras are its iconic features (ii correct). Mughal gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi) line its eastern bank along Zabarwan hills (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — Dal Lake is NOT the largest freshwater lake in India. Wular Lake in J&K itself is larger, and Lake Chilika in Odisha (though brackish) is larger overall.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following hydroelectric projects are located on the Chenab River?

(i) Baglihar
(ii) Salal
(iii) Dulhasti
(iv) Uri-I

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Baglihar (450 MW) is on the Chenab in Doda (i correct). Salal (690 MW) is on the Chenab in Reasi (ii correct). Dulhasti (390 MW) is on the Chenab in Kishtwar (iii correct). Uri-I (iv) is on the JHELUM River, not Chenab. Options B, C, D all incorrectly include Uri-I on the Chenab.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Chenani-Nashri Tunnel (now Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Tunnel) significantly reduced travel time between Jammu and Srinagar.
Reason (R): At approximately 9.2 km, it is India's longest road tunnel and bypasses the difficult Patnitop-Kud section prone to landslides and closures.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the tunnel reduced Jammu-Srinagar travel time by about 2 hours. Reason (R) is correct — at 9.2 km it's India's longest road tunnel and avoids the landslide-prone section. The bypass of difficult terrain (R) explains the time reduction (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the mechanism of the improvement. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist spots with the districts they are located in:

Column I:
(a) Patnitop
(b) Betaab Valley
(c) Sonamarg
(d) Bhaderwah

Column II:
(i) Ganderbal
(ii) Anantnag
(iii) Ramban/Udhampur
(iv) Doda

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Patnitop is in Ramban/Udhampur area on NH-44 (a-iii). Betaab Valley is near Pahalgam in Anantnag (b-ii). Sonamarg is in Ganderbal district on the route to Leh (c-i). Bhaderwah ('Mini Kashmir') is in Doda district (d-iv). Option B swaps Patnitop with Betaab Valley. Option C mismatches Betaab Valley with Sonamarg. Option D incorrectly places Patnitop in Doda.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pakal Dul Hydroelectric Project, one of the largest upcoming projects in J&K, is being built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Pakal Dul HEP (1000 MW planned capacity) is being built on the Marusudar River, a tributary of the Chenab, in Kishtwar district. Jhelum is in the Kashmir Valley. Tawi flows through Jammu city. Indus flows through Ladakh. Only Marusudar hosts this particular project.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Amarnath Cave:

(i) It is located at an altitude of approximately 3,888 metres in Anantnag district.
(ii) The naturally formed ice Shiva Lingam inside the cave is the main attraction.
(iii) The annual Amarnath Yatra takes place during June-August.
(iv) The cave can only be reached by air, with no trekking route available.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The cave is at ~3,888m in Anantnag district (i correct). The natural ice lingam is the primary pilgrimage attraction (ii correct). The yatra occurs in summer months June-August (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the cave is reached by TREKKING routes (Pahalgam and Baltal), not by air. There's no airstrip at the cave.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The total estimated hydroelectric power potential of J&K is approximately:
questions.explanation: J&K has an estimated hydroelectric potential of approximately 20,000 MW, of which only a fraction (about 3,500+ MW) has been harnessed so far. 5,000 MW is too low. 50,000 MW is far too high. 10,000 MW underestimates the total potential.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Hemis Monastery in Ladakh:

(i) It is the largest and wealthiest monastery in Ladakh.
(ii) It belongs to the Drukpa Kagyu lineage of Buddhism.
(iii) The Hemis Festival celebrates the birth of Guru Padmasambhava.
(iv) It was built by Maharaja Gulab Singh in 1846.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hemis is the largest monastery in Ladakh (i correct). It follows the Drukpa Kagyu school (ii correct). The annual Hemis Festival celebrates Guru Padmasambhava (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — Hemis was founded in 1672 by Lama Stagsang Raspa under the patronage of King Sengge Namgyal, NOT by Gulab Singh in 1846.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ Bridge on the USBRL (Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link) is the world's highest railway bridge.
questions.explanation: The Chenab Bridge (also referred to near Anji Khad) on the USBRL is the world's highest railway bridge at 359 metres above the riverbed. Banihal has a tunnel, not the record bridge. Pirpanjal has the longest railway tunnel. Qazigund is a railway station.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following power projects with their installed capacities:

Column I:
(a) Salal
(b) Uri-I
(c) Dulhasti
(d) Uri-II

Column II:
(i) 240 MW
(ii) 480 MW
(iii) 690 MW
(iv) 390 MW

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Salal = 690 MW (a-iii). Uri-I = 480 MW (b-ii). Dulhasti = 390 MW (c-iv). Uri-II = 240 MW (d-i). Option B swaps Salal with Uri-I. Option C mismatches Uri-I with Dulhasti. Option D incorrectly pairs Salal with 240 MW.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are located in the Jammu region (NOT Kashmir Valley)?

(i) Vaishno Devi
(ii) Patnitop
(iii) Bahu Fort
(iv) Gulmarg

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi shrine is in Reasi, Jammu region (i correct). Patnitop hill station is on NH-44 in Jammu division (ii correct). Bahu Fort is in Jammu city on the Tawi (iii correct). Gulmarg (iv) is in the KASHMIR Valley (Baramulla district), NOT the Jammu region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indus Waters Treaty restricts India's use of the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) but allows run-of-the-river hydroelectric projects.
Reason (R): Run-of-the-river projects use natural river flow without significant water storage, thus not materially affecting downstream water availability.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Treaty allocates western rivers to Pakistan but permits India to build run-of-river projects. Reason (R) is correct — run-of-river projects don't store significant water, preserving downstream flow. The minimal impact on flow (R) explains WHY such projects are permitted (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the rationale. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden in Srinagar is significant because:
options: It is Asia's largest tulip garden, blooming in spring (March-April)
It is the oldest Mughal garden in Kashmir
It produces tulips for export to the Netherlands
It was built by Emperor Akbar in the 16th century
questions.correctAnswer: It is Asia's largest tulip garden, blooming in spring (March-April)
questions.explanation: The Tulip Garden (opened 2007) is Asia's largest tulip garden with over 1.5 million bulbs of various varieties, blooming in spring. It is NOT a Mughal garden — it was developed recently. It doesn't produce for export commercially. It was NOT built by Akbar — it's a modern garden on the foothills of the Zabarwan range.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Srinagar-Leh Highway (NH-1):

(i) It passes through Zoji La Pass at approximately 3,528 metres.
(ii) It remains closed during winter due to heavy snowfall.
(iii) Sonamarg is the last major town before Zoji La on this route.
(iv) The highway is approximately 100 km long.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The highway crosses Zoji La at ~3,528m (i correct). It closes in winter (November-May typically) due to snow (ii correct). Sonamarg is the last major settlement before Zoji La on the Kashmir side (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the Srinagar-Leh highway is approximately 434 km long, NOT 100 km.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tunnels in J&K with their primary purpose:

Column I:
(a) Jawahar Tunnel (Banihal)
(b) Chenani-Nashri Tunnel
(c) Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel
(d) Z-Morh Tunnel

Column II:
(i) Connects Jammu to Srinagar highway (bypasses Kud-Patnitop)
(ii) Road tunnel connecting Kashmir Valley to Jammu via Banihal Pass
(iii) Provides all-weather road connectivity to Sonamarg
(iv) Railway link through Pir Panjal range

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jawahar Tunnel connects Jammu to Kashmir via the Banihal Pass road (a-ii). Chenani-Nashri bypasses the Kud-Patnitop section on NH-44 (b-i). Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel is for the USBRL rail link (c-iv). Z-Morh Tunnel provides year-round road access to Sonamarg (d-iii). Option B swaps Jawahar with Chenani-Nashri. Option C mismatches Chenani-Nashri with Z-Morh. Option D incorrectly places Jawahar as railway.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Manasbal Lake, known as the 'Supreme Gem of All Kashmir Lakes', is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Manasbal Lake is located in Ganderbal district, about 30 km north of Srinagar. It is known for its lotus blooms and clear water. Srinagar has Dal Lake. Baramulla has Wular Lake. Bandipora is also near Wular but Manasbal falls in Ganderbal.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the impact of power projects on J&K's economy:

(i) They provide electricity for domestic and industrial consumption.
(ii) They generate revenue through sale of surplus power to other states.
(iii) They create employment during construction and operation.
(iv) All the electricity generated in J&K is consumed locally with no surplus.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Power projects provide local electricity (i correct). Surplus power is sold to the national grid generating revenue (ii correct). Projects create jobs (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — J&K produces surplus power (especially in summer with high river flows) that IS sold to other states. In fact, J&K ALSO purchases power in winter when generation drops.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sonamarg is called the 'Gateway to Ladakh' from the Kashmir side.
Reason (R): Sonamarg is the last major town on the Srinagar-Leh highway before the road crosses the Zoji La Pass into the Ladakh region.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Sonamarg is known as the gateway to Ladakh. Reason (R) is correct — its location as the last town before Zoji La on the Srinagar-Leh road makes it the entry point for the Ladakh journey. The geographical position (R) explains the gateway designation (A). Option B is wrong because (R) explains why. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel on the USBRL project is approximately how long?
questions.explanation: The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel (also called Banihal-Qazigund tunnel) is approximately 11.215 km long, making it India's longest railway tunnel. 9.2 km is the length of Chenani-Nashri road tunnel. 5.5 km is too short. 15 km is too long for this specific tunnel.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are popular trekking destinations in J&K?

(i) Tarsar-Marsar trek
(ii) Great Lakes trek
(iii) Kolahoi Glacier trek
(iv) Rajpath trek

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Tarsar-Marsar is a famous twin-lake trek in Aru Valley (i correct). The Kashmir Great Lakes trek covers alpine lakes (ii correct). Kolahoi Glacier trek goes to the Kolahoi glacier from Pahalgam (iii correct). 'Rajpath trek' (iv) is NOT a J&K trek — Rajpath refers to the ceremonial road in New Delhi (now Kartavya Path).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Wular Lake:

(i) It is the largest freshwater lake in India.
(ii) It is located in Bandipora district.
(iii) The Jhelum River flows through it.
(iv) It has been declared a Ramsar Wetland Site.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All statements are correct. Wular is India's largest freshwater lake (i). It's in Bandipora district (ii). The Jhelum flows through it (iii). It was designated a Ramsar site in 1990 (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Baglihar Dam dispute between India and Pakistan was resolved by:
options: A Neutral Expert appointed under the Indus Waters Treaty
questions.correctAnswer: A Neutral Expert appointed under the Indus Waters Treaty
questions.explanation: The Baglihar dispute was referred to a Neutral Expert (Professor Raymond Lafitte of Switzerland) under the Treaty's dispute resolution mechanism, who gave his verdict in 2007. The ICJ was not involved. The UNSC did not adjudicate. While bilateral talks occurred, the formal resolution was through the Neutral Expert mechanism.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is a famous hill station in the Jammu region often called 'Mini Kashmir' due to its lush green meadows.
questions.explanation: Bhaderwah in Doda district is called 'Mini Kashmir' or 'Chhota Kashmir' for its scenic meadows and pleasant climate. Patnitop is also a hill station but isn't called Mini Kashmir. Katra is the base town for Vaishno Devi. Samba is a plains district — not a hill station.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following religious/tourist sites with their significance:

Column I:
(a) Hazratbal Shrine
(b) Shankaracharya Temple
(c) Raghunath Temple
(d) Charar-i-Sharief

Column II:
(i) One of the largest temple complexes in North India, Jammu
(ii) Houses a relic believed to be of Prophet Muhammad
(iii) Shrine of Sufi saint Sheikh Noor-ud-din, Budgam
(iv) Ancient Shiva temple on a hilltop in Srinagar

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Hazratbal houses the holy relic (Moi-e-Muqaddas) believed to be Prophet Muhammad's hair (a-ii). Shankaracharya Temple is on Takht-i-Sulaiman hill, dedicated to Lord Shiva (b-iv). Raghunath Temple is among North India's largest temple complexes in Jammu (c-i). Charar-i-Sharief is the shrine of Nund Rishi (Sheikh Noor-ud-din) in Budgam (d-iii). Option B swaps Hazratbal with Shankaracharya. Option C mismatches Shankaracharya with Raghunath. Option D incorrectly pairs Hazratbal with Charar-i-Sharief.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Zoji La Tunnel project aims to provide year-round connectivity between Srinagar and Ladakh.
Reason (R): Currently, the Srinagar-Leh highway closes for 4-5 months every winter due to heavy snowfall at Zoji La Pass, cutting off Ladakh from Kashmir.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Zoji La Tunnel will enable all-weather connectivity. Reason (R) is correct — winter closures of 4-5 months isolate Ladakh. The seasonal isolation described in (R) is the problem the tunnel in (A) aims to solve. Option B is wrong because (R) explains the necessity. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous floating vegetable market on Dal Lake operates during:
options: All day from 9 AM to 5 PM
questions.explanation: The floating market (locally called 'Raadh') on Dal Lake operates in the predawn/early morning hours (around 4-6 AM). Vendors gather on shikaras to trade vegetables and flowers. It does not operate in the afternoon, evening, or as a standard 9-5 market. The early timing is part of its unique character.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the UDHAMPUR-SRINAGAR-BARAMULLA Rail Link (USBRL):

(i) It will connect the Kashmir Valley to the Indian railway network for the first time.
(ii) It includes the Chenab Bridge, the world's highest railway bridge.
(iii) It includes the Pir Panjal Tunnel, India's longest railway tunnel.
(iv) The entire project was completed and opened in 2020.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: USBRL provides the first rail link to Kashmir Valley (i correct). It includes the Chenab Bridge at 359m height (ii correct). The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel at 11.2 km is India's longest (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the USBRL project was NOT fully completed by 2020; sections are still under construction as of 2024-2025.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the installed capacity (in MW) of selected hydroelectric projects in J&K:

Salal → Chenab, 690
Uri-I → Jhelum, 480
Dulhasti → Chenab, 390
Kishanganga → Kishanganga, 330
Uri-II → Jhelum, 240

What is the total installed capacity of projects on the Chenab River from the above list?
questions.explanation: Chenab projects from the list: Salal (690 MW) + Dulhasti (390 MW) = 1,080 MW. Option 1,320 MW incorrectly adds Kishanganga. Option 690 MW counts only Salal. Option 1,560 MW adds all projects incorrectly.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dachigam National Park near Srinagar is primarily famous for the conservation of:
questions.explanation: Dachigam is home to the critically endangered Hangul (Kashmir Stag/Cervus hanglu), the only surviving species of red deer in India. Snow Leopards are found at higher altitudes in Hemis National Park, Ladakh. Bengal Tigers are in Jim Corbett and Ranthambore. Asiatic Lions are in Gir, Gujarat.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows tourist arrivals to J&K over recent years:

2018 → 80
2019 → 52
2020 → 12
2022 → 189
2023 → 210

In which year was the percentage decline from the previous listed year the greatest?
questions.explanation: 2019 decline: (80-52)/80 × 100 = 35% drop. 2020 decline: (52-12)/52 × 100 = 76.9% drop (COVID + lockdown). 2022 showed massive INCREASE (not decline) from 2020. 2023 also increased. The 2020 drop of ~77% (due to COVID-19) was the greatest percentage decline.
